**Jupiter** is the fifth [planet](/wiki/Planet "Planet") from the [Sun](/wiki/Sun "Sun"), and the [largest in the Solar System](/wiki/List_of_Solar_System_objects_by_size "List of Solar System objects by size"). It is a [gas giant](/wiki/Gas_giant "Gas giant") with a [mass](/wiki/Jupiter_mass "Jupiter mass") nearly 2.5 times that of all the other planets in the [Solar System](/wiki/Solar_System "Solar System") combined and slightly less than one-thousandth the mass of the Sun. Its diameter is 11 times that of [Earth](/wiki/Earth "Earth") and a tenth that of the Sun. Jupiter orbits the Sun at a distance of 5.20 [AU](/wiki/Astronomical_unit "Astronomical unit") (778.5 [Gm](/wiki/Gigametre "Gigametre")), with an [orbital period](/wiki/Orbital_period "Orbital period") of 11.86 [years](/wiki/Julian_year_(astronomy) "Julian year (astronomy)"). It is the [third-brightest natural object](/wiki/List_of_brightest_natural_objects_in_the_sky "List of brightest natural objects in the sky") in the Earth's [night sky](/wiki/Night_sky "Night sky"), after the [Moon](/wiki/Moon "Moon") and [Venus](/wiki/Venus "Venus"), and has been observed since [prehistoric times](/wiki/Prehistoric_times "Prehistoric times"). Its name derives from that of [Jupiter](/wiki/Jupiter_(god) "Jupiter (god)"), the chief deity of [ancient Roman religion](/wiki/Ancient_Roman_religion "Ancient Roman religion").

Hajin Lee, a former professional Go player, described this documentary as being "beautifully filmed". In addition to the story itself, the feelings and atmosphere were also conveyed through different scene arrangements. For example, the close-up shots of Lee Sedol when he realizes that the AlphaGo AI is intelligent, the atmospheric scene of the Korean commentator's distress and affliction following the first defeat, and the tension being held inside the room. The documentary also tells a story by describing the background of AlphaGo technology and the customs of the Korean Go community. She suggests some areas to be covered additionally. For instance, the details of the AI prior to AlphaGo, the confidence and pride of the professional Go players, and the shifting of perspective to the Go AI between and after the match as "If anything could be added, I would include information about the primitive level of top Go A.I.s before AlphaGo, and more about professional Go players' lives and pride, to provide more context for Lee Sedol's pre-match confidence, and Go players' changing perception of AlphaGo as the match advanced".[[93]](#cite_note-93)(Lee, 2017).

Fan Hui, a professional Go player, and former player with AlphaGo said that "DeepMind had trained AlphaGo by showing it many strong amateur games of Go to develop its understanding of how a human plays before challenging it to play versions of itself thousands of times, a novel form of reinforcement learning which had given it the ability to rival an expert human. History had been made, and centuries of received learning overturned in the process. The program was free to learn the game for itself.[[94]](#cite_note-:1-94)

In early 1992 it was confirmed that Soviet forces in Cuba had already received tactical nuclear warheads for their [artillery rockets](/wiki/Rocket_artillery "Rocket artillery") and [Il-28 bombers](/wiki/Ilyushin_Il-28 "Ilyushin Il-28") when the crisis broke.[[221]](#cite_note-aca-224) Castro stated that he would have recommended their use if the US had invaded, even if Cuba was destroyed.[[221]](#cite_note-aca-224)

Fifty years after the crisis, [Graham Allison](/wiki/Graham_Allison "Graham Allison") wrote:

> Fifty years ago, the Cuban Missile Crisis brought the world to the brink of nuclear disaster. During the standoff, US President John F. Kennedy thought the chance of escalation to war was "between 1 in 3 and even", and what we have learned in later decades has done nothing to lengthen those odds. We now know, for example, that in addition to nuclear-armed ballistic missiles, the Soviet Union had deployed 100 tactical nuclear weapons to Cuba, and the local Soviet commander there could have launched these weapons without additional codes or commands from Moscow. The US air strike and invasion that were scheduled for the third week of the confrontation would likely have triggered a nuclear response against American ships and troops, and perhaps even [Miami](/wiki/Miami "Miami"). The resulting war might have led to the deaths of over 100 million Americans and over 100 million Russians.[[222]](#cite_note-225)[[223]](#cite_note-226)

[BBC](/wiki/BBC "BBC") journalist Joe Matthews published the story, on 13 October 2012, after news of the 100 tactical nuclear warheads mentioned by Graham Allison in the excerpt above.[[224]](#cite_note-MatthewsBBC20121013-227) Khrushchev feared that Castro's hurt pride and widespread Cuban indignation over the concessions he had made to Kennedy might lead to a breakdown of the agreement between the Soviet Union and the United States. To prevent this, Khrushchev decided to offer to give Cuba more than 100 tactical nuclear weapons that had been shipped there with the long-range missiles but, crucially, had escaped the notice of US intelligence.

Main article: [Sport in Vatican City](/wiki/Sport_in_Vatican_City "Sport in Vatican City")

The Vatican City is not a member of the [International Olympic Committee](/wiki/International_Olympic_Committee "International Olympic Committee") and does not compete in the [Olympic Games](/wiki/Olympic_Games "Olympic Games"), though it has participated in some international sporting events, including the [World Cycling Championships](/wiki/World_Cycling_Championships "World Cycling Championships"),[[160]](#cite_note-Pender_2022-173) the [Championships of the Small States of Europe](/wiki/Championships_of_the_Small_States_of_Europe "Championships of the Small States of Europe") and the [Mediterranean Games](/wiki/Mediterranean_Games "Mediterranean Games").[[161]](#cite_note-Med_Games-174) Vatican City has its own athletics association, [Athletica Vaticana](/wiki/Athletica_Vaticana "Athletica Vaticana").[[162]](#cite_note-LOsservatore_Romano_2023_a014-175)

[Football](/wiki/Association_football "Association football") in Vatican City is organized by the [Vatican Amateur Sports Association](/wiki/Vatican_Amateur_Sports_Association "Vatican Amateur Sports Association"), which holds the national championship, called the [Vatican City Championship](/wiki/Vatican_City_Championship "Vatican City Championship"), with eight teams, including, for example, the Swiss Guard's [FC Guardia](/wiki/FC_Guardia "FC Guardia") and police and museum guard teams.[[163]](#cite_note-176) The association organizes the [Coppa Sergio Valci](/wiki/Coppa_Sergio_Valci "Coppa Sergio Valci") and the [Vatican Supercoppa](/wiki/Supercoppa_(Vatican_City) "Supercoppa (Vatican City)"). It controls the [Vatican City national football team](/wiki/Vatican_City_national_football_team "Vatican City national football team"), which is neither affiliated with [UEFA](/wiki/UEFA "UEFA") nor [FIFA](/wiki/FIFA "FIFA").
